missionPremise: DO NOT MAKE THE STORE THE PREDICATE (OPS-24 Law 1, dispatch 'Seven laws' 1, and A-183): the customer predicate is `scripts/surface-probe.mjs` driven with a real address, not a stage's private check and not a store-reading instrument - 'a store-reading instrument is never the customer predicate', because the factory-store and atoms-store instruments were green through the whole 2026-09-15 map incident. This lane is therefore the customer leg of the Phase 0 exit (scope rev 4 section 5, exit condition 2): the probe must grade the THREE CUSTOMER SURFACES - the map payload, the MCP, and the PDF - over the delivered bucket fixture list, so that a county's completion is a thing a customer can observe rather than a ledger count. Two further standing rulings bound what the grading may treat as correct: ENVELOPE DRAWN, FIGURE REFUSED (operator 2026-09-11, _decisions/2026-09-11_ruling_b_reversed_polygon_only.md) - the modelled envelope MAY draw wherever a district and a setback table exist, but buildable area and percent stay refused until a verdict-backed envelope atom exists (A-180), with the MCP payload and PDF not enforcing that today (P-249, P-261) - and MOST-CURRENT SOURCE WINS (operator 2026-09-11) with the P-178 vintage rule, which makes an undated setback citation a conflict row rather than a silent pick. The dispatch hands this lane two findings measured by the integration seat as REQUIRED CASES, and they are the reason the instrument must compare surfaces against EACH OTHER and not each surface against itself: a ruled table described as 'unruled' on one surface while another draws it, and two impervious figures under one customer idea.

theStandard.cardSpec: _inbox/2026-09-16_scaleup-le_card_spec.md - the acceptance standard the buckets are graded against (what a property card, the MCP and a PDF must show).
theStandard.fixtureList: _inbox/2026-09-16_scaleup-le_fixture_list.json, COMMITTED INTO THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN TREE as scripts/fixtures/surface-probe/ops24-fixture-list.json so the grading is traceable to the list it graded.
theStandard.instrument: scripts/surface-probe.mjs (OPS-23's predicate with its own self-test and committed fixtures). Its exit codes and its MEASURED/OBSERVED labelling are kept: 0 = decided and clean, 1 = a predicate FAILED, 2 = the run could not decide (a refused or unreachable leg) while --allow-unmeasured was not passed.
theStandard.rowsCarried: P-254 (the OPS-24 legs) plus predicates for P-303 and P-304, which the dispatch asks this lane to carry for the lanes landing now.

bucketPopulation.selectionRule: ONE fixture graded per bucket, first by OPS24_CATEGORY_PRIORITY [fx_codified, fx_pud, fx_district_miss, fx_no_table, fx_vacant, fx_any]; the buckets' remaining fixtures are REPORTED as ungraded slots rather than dropped, so the denominator is visible (45 graded of 122 offered, 77 ungraded, at the close).
bucketPopulation.divergenceFromTheDispatchProse: The dispatch and the plan both say 'the 39-bucket fixture list'; the delivered list at _inbox/2026-09-16_scaleup-le_fixture_list.json contains 45 buckets over the six Phase 0 counties. A number that should agree and does not is a finding, so it is recorded here and in the close rather than rounded: this instrument grades ALL 45 as delivered, counts them, and the count is reported with its source (the list's own sha256 above). The '39' is not silently adopted and not silently corrected.
bucketPopulation.fixtureSlotCountingRule: A slot is one fx_<category> key present in a bucket object. A fixture id that appears under two categories in one bucket (e.g. 48453:352594 under fx_codified and fx_vacant) counts as TWO slots offered but ONE parcel - which is why 122 slots resolve to 100 unique fixture ids and 52 unique probed parcels.

mapPayload.whatIsRead: baseFacts (apn, landUse, acreage, situsAddress/situsCity/situsState), zoning (district, jurisdictionKey, provenance), envelope (status, setbacks, approximate, provisional, disclosure, citationUrl, maxImperviousPct), facetCoverage, recordRailStates, cityLimitsFact, and the envelope/impervious facts used by the required cases
mapPayload.grading: the bucket verdict's map half; a payload that does not answer makes the bucket UNMEASURED, never PASS

drawRoute.route: POST https://smartsite.cloud/api/spine/cortex/api/brokerage/v1/place/buildable-envelope (the panel's own draw route, used as the SECOND surface the panel can contradict)
drawRoute.authorisation: anonymous through the same public proxy
drawRoute.inputContract: composedAddress first, then recordPoint, then the bare situs - and the response is REJECTED as evidence for a different parcel, so a finding can never be sourced from a wrong resolution
drawRoute.whyItIsALeg: XD-2/X5 and P-303 are precisely 'the panel declines what its own route draws', which is unobservable without calling the route

mcp.route: POST https://smartsite-mcp-tds7av26va-uc.a.run.app/mcp, JSON-RPC `initialize` then `tools/call get_smart_site` at node depth
mcp.authorisation: OAuth Bearer via SURFACE_PROBE_MCP_TOKEN (the gate refuses a service Bearer; see credentialPlan)
mcp.transport: SSE or plain JSON frames, parsed by parseMcpBody; a gate refusal with no result is treated as NO SESSION, never as a result

pdf.authorisation: the six gate-front headers x-hauska-product, x-hauska-tenant-id, x-hauska-package-id, x-hauska-gate-credential-id, x-hauska-access-tier, x-hauska-request-id, plus a Bearer key (HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_KEY)
pdf.gradedAs: pdfSurfaceState, four states: SERVED, NOT-BUILT (the export answers `never-requested`), FAILED, UNREACHED (the leg could not be authorised or reached)

credentialPlan.pdf: HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_KEY read at run time from Secret Manager in project hauska-prod-497015 (`gcloud secrets versions access latest`) and passed only through the environment; it is never printed, never written to an artifact, and never committed. A test-only scratch script may print its LENGTH, never its value.
credentialPlan.mcp: SURFACE_PROBE_MCP_TOKEN is NOT available to this lane. That is a REFUSAL to declare, not a gap to paper over: the leg is attempted, the gate's own words are recorded (see refusalIsAResult), and the MCP half of every judgement is UNMEASURED. The dispatch permits this explicitly ('A leg that cannot be run is a REFUSAL (exit 2) or enters through --observations labelled OBSERVED. Never a pass it did not measure').
credentialPlan.refusalIsAResult: A refused leg is recorded with the gate's verbatim reason and labels the surface UNMEASURED - it never yields a PASS, and it never disappears from the artifact.

defectLedgerDesign.whatItIs: The open-defect COUNT that the Phase 0 exit reads (dispatch 'What to build 4'), over the XD and X defect lists in plan section 4.5. Each defect carries its id, its owning row, an optional grader, and a verdict of OPEN / CLOSED / UNMEASURED with the basis and the parcel hits.
defectLedgerDesign.threeStatesNotTwo: A defect with NO grader in this instrument is UNMEASURED with the row that owns it named - never counted CLOSED (an unmeasured defect is not a closed one) and never counted OPEN (nothing observed it). This is what keeps the count honest: 23 defects, of which 11 graded, 5 closed, 7 owned elsewhere.
defectLedgerDesign.verdictVsDefect: The bucket VERDICT (PASS/FAIL/UNMEASURED) and the defect LEDGER are deliberately different instruments with different jobs, and the split was forced by measurement: the first draft counted XD-11 (a setback citation with no effective date) as a bucket VIOLATION, and it fired on 25 of 45 buckets - one class drowning every other result and hiding both required cases. XD-11 is a real defect, but it is a defect OF THE VINTAGE RULE, so it now enters the ledger (and is still printed per bucket under 'defects recorded') while the bucket verdict is decided by the customer-facing rules the card spec names. The split is stated in the artifact, not silent: defectClasses and violationClasses are both emitted, and every recorded defect names its class.
defectLedgerDesign.countingRule: measuredOn is the number of subject-parcels on which the grader could reach a verdict at all (e.g. XD-7 on 45 of 52: it cannot be measured on a payload that carries nothing to be addressed). hits is the number of those subjects still showing the defect. Every count in the close travels with these two numbers.

falsifiersPreRegistered.1: A fixture known to fail today reads FAIL. Named BEFORE the run: 48453:367134 (5833 Taylor Draper Cv, Austin) on the cross-surface envelope-reason check, which the dispatch hands this lane as a required case. Any others found live are named as new, not presented as predicted.
falsifiersPreRegistered.2: A fixture known to pass reads PASS, and a copy of it with ONE asserted field altered reads FAIL - i.e. the check is proven NON-VACUOUS by its own self-test rather than asserted to be. Pre-registered method: `node scripts/surface-probe.mjs --self-test`, whose paired cases (fire/do-not-fire on the same input with one field changed) are the evidence, since a self-test that only ever passes proves nothing.
falsifiersPreRegistered.3: With a leg's credential withheld, that leg REFUSES and the run does not report a pass for it. Pre-registered as TWO observations, because they are two different claims: (a) the withheld leg is absent-or-refused and never a PASS; (b) the instrument's exit code distinguishes 'could not decide' (2) from 'decided and failed' (1) - and per scripts/surface-probe.mjs:2359 a measured FAIL outranks an unmeasured refusal by design, so exit 1 on a run that both fails and cannot decide is CORRECT, not a failed refusal test.
falsifiersPreRegistered.notPreRegisteredAndSaidSo: The two findings this lane contributes beyond the dispatch (the no-location class, and an address absence that carries no basis) were NOT predicted. They are reported as discoveries with their populations, not as confirmed predictions.

outOfScopeNamedAtCp1: The ledger leg (P-253), the coverage leg (P-210), the road residual (P-264) and the operator's walk: the other four legs of the same Phase 0 exit, each another lane. This lane is the customer leg only.
No product repository is edited and nothing is deployed: every defect this lane finds is a FINDING (the dispatch's 'Do not'). The instrument lives in doc_repo.
No store is read or written, and no privileged path is used: every credential here reaches a PUBLIC customer surface, and the fixtures are graded the way a customer reaches them.

The PDF's CONTENT and the MCP's schema beyond the graded surfaces: this lane grades whether the three surfaces AGREE and whether each one withholds what a ruling says it must withhold, not whether a PDF's prose is good.
